questions.question: The festival of Makar Sankranti is devoted to which of the following gods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Makar Sankranti** is a Hindu festival that is celebrated across** India, Nepal and Bangladesh.**
 
• It is also known as **Uttarayan **and is dedicated to the **Sun God, Surya.**
 
• The festival is observed on **January 14th** every year and marks the transition of the Sun from the **Tropic of Cancer to the Tropic of Capricorn.**
 
• During this time, people take holy dips in rivers, offer prayers to the Sun God and indulge in traditional foods like** tilgul, laddoo and khichdi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vishnu** is a **Hindu God** who is also widely worshipped in India. 
 
• **Indra** is a deity associated with **thunder and rain** and is not connected with Makar Sankranti.
 
• **Shiva** is one of the **principal deities** in Hinduism.

questions.question: Which of the following is a tertiary consumer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snake.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** tertiary consumer** is an organism that feeds on **secondary consumers.**
 
• In this case, the **snake** feeds on **frogs** or other small animals that** feed on insects or plants.**
 
• **Grass** is a **primary producer **and forms the base of the **food chain.**
 
• It is eaten by **primary consumers** such as** grasshoppers.**
 
• A **frog** is a **secondary consumer** as it feeds on insects such as **grasshoppers **or other small animals that feed on plants.
 
• Grasshopper is also a **primary consumer** that feeds on grass or other plants.
 
• Understanding the** trophic levels in a food chain** is important for understanding the **flow of energy and nutrients** in an ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grass **is an important food source for many herbivores such as** cows, sheep, and deer.**
 
• **Snakes** are **carnivorous** and feed on a variety of prey such as **rodents, birds, and other small animals.**
 
 
• They play an important role in controlling the population of their **prey and maintaining the balance **in the ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Frogs** are **amphibians** that are found in many different habitats such as **ponds, lakes, and streams.**
 
 
• They are important predators of insects and other small animals and are also an important food source for many larger predators such as **birds and snakes.**
 
 
 
• **Grasshoppers** are **herbivorous insects** that feed on a variety of plants such as **grass, leaves, and flowers.**
 
 
• They are an important food source for many animals such as **birds, rodents, and reptiles.**

questions.question: Which of the following period is referred as the period of population explosion in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951 - 1981.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The period of **population explosion** in India is referred to as **1951-1981**.
 
• During this period, India's population grew at an** unprecedented rate**, increasing from around** 361 million in 1951** to over **846 million in 1981**.
 
• This period was marked by several factors, including improvements in **healthcare and sanitation, increased agricultural productivity,** and a **decline in infant mortality rates.**
 
• The population explosion had several** social and economic consequences**, including increased pressure on **resources, urbanization, and poverty.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1901-1921** was a period of relatively** slow population growth** in India, with the population increasing from around** 238 million to 251 million.**
 
• **1921-1951** was a period of **moderate population growth**, with the population increasing from around **251 million to 361 million.**

questions.question: Which of the following ancient site is NOT situated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrgarh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mehrgarh** is not situated in India but in present-day **Pakistan.**
 
• **Hunsgi** is an ancient site located in the state of **Karnataka**, India, known for its** Paleolithic and Neolithic **stone tools and artifacts.
 
• **Hallur **is an archaeological site located in the state of **Karnataka, India**, known for its **megalithic** burials and artifacts from the Iron Age.
 
• **Inamgaon **is an ancient site located in the state of **Maharashtra, **India, known for its** Chalcolithic and Bronze Age **settlements and artifacts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mehrgarh** is an archaeological site located in the **Balochistan province of Pakistan**, known for its Neolithic and Bronze Age settlements and artifacts.
 
• The site was discovered in **1974 **and is considered one of the most **important archaeological sites** in South Asia for understanding the early human settlements and the development of **agriculture and civilization.**
 
• Mehrgarh was inhabited from around **7000 BCE to 2000 BCE** and is known for its advanced **metallurgy, pottery, and textile industries.**
 
• The site has also yielded evidence of early domestication of animals such as **sheep, goats, and cattle, and the cultivation of crops such as wheat, barley, and lentils.**

questions.question: The objective of Simon Commission was to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decide India's Political future.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **objective of Simon Commission **was to decide **India's Political future.**
 
• The Simon Commission was appointed by the **British government in 1927** to review the working of the **Government of India Act 1919** and suggest reforms.
 
• The Commission was headed by **Sir John Simon,** a British politician, and included **six other members**, all of whom were British.
 
• The Commission was met with **widespread protests in India** as it did not have any Indian members and was seen as an attempt by the British government to further **strengthen** their hold on India.
 
• The Commission submitted its **report in May 1930,** which recommended limited reforms in the** central government and provincial governments.** However, the recommendations **were not accepted** by the Indian political parties as they did not address the demand for Indian independence.
 
• The failure of the Simon Commission led to the formation of the** Round Table Conferences,** which were aimed at finding a solution to India's political future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Commission did recommend the establishment of a **separate education department** in the central government to oversee education in India.
 
• Commission did recommend measures to improve the** economic conditions of the people in India,** such as the establishment of a **central bank** and the development of** agriculture and industry.**

questions.question: Which act of British Parliament was also known as East India Company Act 1793?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Charter Act, 1793.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Charter Act, 1793** was also known as the** East India Company Act 1793** because it renewed the company's charter for another **20 years.**
 
• The Act also** increased** the **power of the Governor-General** and established a **Board of Control** to oversee the company's affairs in India.
 
• The Act also prohibited company officials from engaging in** private trade** and required them to disclose their **private assets.**
 
• The Act also made provisions for the** establishment of a college in Calcutta **to train Indian civil servants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Government of India Act, 1793 **was an act of the British Parliament that established the** Governor-General of India** as the head of the British administration in India.
 
• The **Regulating Act, 1793 **was the first major British law on India that established a** Supreme Court in Calcutta** and a Board of Control to oversee the company's affairs in India.
 
• The** Indian Councils Act, 1793 **was an act of the British Parliament that expanded the role of Indians in the administration of India by allowing them to become members of the **Governor-General's council.**

questions.question: The largest ocean on Earth is the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pacific Ocean.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pacific Ocean **covers an area of about **63.8 million square miles,** which is larger than the combined area of all the other oceans on Earth.
 
• It stretches from the **Arctic Ocean **in the north to the **Southern Ocean** in the south and from the **coasts of Asia and Australia** in the west to the Americas in the east.
 
• The Pacific Ocean is also the** deepest ocean on Earth**, with an average depth of over **12,000 feet.**
 
• It contains several of the world's largest and deepest trenches, including the **Mariana Trench, **which is the deepest point on Earth at a depth of **36,070 feet.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Atlantic Ocean** is the** second-largest ocean **on Earth, covering an area of about **41.1 million square miles.**

 
 
• It is also **shallower than the Pacific Ocean,** with an average depth of around **10,900 feet.**
 
 
 
• The** Arctic Ocean** is the **smallest and shallowest ocean** on Earth, covering an area of about** 5.4 million square miles.**
 
 
• It is located at the **North Pole** and is mostly covered by ice throughout the year.
 
 
 
• The **Indian Ocean** is the** third-largest ocean** on Earth, covering an area of about **28.4 million square miles.**
 
 
• It is located between **Africa, Asia, Australia,** and the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: What does it mean when an object has a positive charge?

options.text: It has more electrons than protons
It has more protons than electrons
It has more neutrons than electrons
It has more neutrons than protons

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has more protons than electrons.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object has a** positive charge**, it means that it has** lost electrons** and has **more protons** than electrons.
 
• Protons are** positively charged particles** found in the** nucleus of an atom** while electrons are **negatively charged particles** that orbit around the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Having **more electrons than protons** would result in a **negative charge.**
 
• **Neutrons **are** neutral particles **and do not contribute to the **charge of an atom.**
 
• **Number of neutrons** does not affect the charge of an atom.
 
• It's important to note that the charge of an object can be **positive, negative, or neutral,** depending on the balance of protons and electrons.

questions.question: Insufficient exposure to sunlight causes deficiency of which vitamin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin D **is known as the** sunshine vitamin** because it is produced by the body when the skin is exposed to sunlight.
 
• Insufficient exposure to sunlight can cause a **deficienc****y** of this vitamin.
 
• Vitamin D is important for the absorption of** calcium and phosphorus**, which are essential for **strong bones and teeth.**
 
• A deficiency of **vitamin D** can lead to bone diseases such as rickets in **children and osteomalacia** in adults.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Vitamin E is an **antioxidant** that protects cells from damage, while** vitamin K **is important for **blood clotting.**
 
• **Vitamin A **is important for **vision, immune function**, and **skin health.**
 
• It is found in animal products such as** liver and dairy,** as well as in plant foods such as** carrots and spinach.**
 
• **Vitamin C** is an antioxidant that is important for **immune function, skin health, and wound healing.**
 
• It is found in** citrus fruits, berries, and leafy greens.**

questions.question: Article 40 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.

options.text: Uniform civil code for the citizens

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Organisation of village panchayats.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 40** of the Indian constitution is related to the organization of** village panchayats.**
 
• This article directs the state to take steps to** organize village panchayats** and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as **units of self-government.**
 
• The main objective of this article is to promote** local self-governance and decentralization of power.**
 
• The village panchayats are responsible for the** economic and social development** of the village community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protection of life** is covered under** Article 21** of the Indian constitution, which guarantees the** right to life and personal liberty.**
 
• **Uniform Civil Code** is not explicitly mentioned in the Indian constitution, although there is a** directive principle (Article 44)** that states that the state shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India.
 
• **Freedom to manage religious affairs** is covered under **Article 26** of the Indian constitution, which guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice and propagate religion.

questions.question: Around 2000 years ago ______ became the second capital of the Kushanas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mathura.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Kushanas** were a **Central Asian dynasty** that ruled over a vast empire in **South Asia f**rom the** 1st to the 3rd century CE.**
 
• Mathura, located in **present-day Uttar Pradesh, **was an important center of trade, art, and religion during the Kushana period.
 
• It was also a strategic location for controlling the **Gangetic plains** and the trade routes to the northwest.
 
• The Kushanas made **Mathura** their **second capital** after **Peshawar** (in present-day Pakistan).
 
• They built several palaces, temples, and other structures in Mathura, which became a** thriving urban center** under their patronage.
 
• Some of the notable Kushana rulers who resided in Mathura were **Kanishka, Huvishka, and Vasudeva.**
 
• They were known for their patronage of **Buddhism and other religions**, as well as their **military and diplomatic campaigns.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Patliputra** (present-day Patna) was the capital of several ancient Indian empires, including the **Mauryas and the Guptas.**
 
• It was an important **political and cultural center** in North India.
 
• **Madurai,** located in present-day **Tamil Nadu,** was a prominent city in **South India**, known for its **rich history, art, and literature.**
 
• **Vaishali**, located in present-day** Bihar, **was an ancient republic that played a significant role in the spread of **Buddhism in India.**
